Subject: Brightline: RCA & tactical action plan for June 29 outage

Alyssa — thanks again for your patience while our team completed the internal review. Attached is a concise RCA and a CSV timeline for the June 29 incident (files: Brightline_RCA_2026-06-30.pdf, event_timeline_20260629.csv). Below is a short summary and the immediate actions we are taking.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Impact: Transient availability degradation of the inference endpoint used by Brightline between 2026-06-29T18:02:00Z and 2026-06-29T18:47:00Z. ~9% of requests returned 5xx errors; latency spikes for ~14% of traffic.
- Root cause: A rollout of a kernel-selection optimizer was unintentionally pushed to a subset of Dedicated nodes with an incompatible microcode path; as sequence lengths exceeded internal thresholds the runtime hit an error path that triggered resource starvation and evictions.
- Mitigation: We rolled back the rollout at 18:47Z and applied a targeted hotfix to prevent re-entry into the bad kernel path.

Immediate action items (owner / ETA)
- Patch: apply conservative kernel-selection guard to all Dedicated pools (Jonas / completed 2026-06-29 19:10Z).
- Validation: expanded smoke test to include long-sequence churn test case used by Brightline (Marissa / 2026-07-01).
- Observability: surfaced a new alert on kernel-selection failures and increased retention of trace samples for 72 hours (Priyom / completed 2026-06-29 20:00Z).
- Postmortem follow-ups: schedule technical deep-dive with Brightline engineering to walk timeline and logs (Marissa / proposed 2026-07-02).

Attachments: Brightline_RCA_2026-06-30.pdf (3 pages executive summary + detailed timeline), event_timeline_20260629.csv (per-node events), mitigation_patch.diff (diff of guard change).

We want to be transparent about impact and our fixes; please let us know if you need additional evidence (audit logs, specific request ids). If you’re available, Marissa will propose a 60-minute deep-dive for your team and our engineering leads to walk the logs and planned mitigations.

Best,
Priyom

Alyssa / team — quick technical clarification and an updated action we committed after the initial hotfix.

Clarification on root cause: the kernel-selection optimizer relied on a fallback path that assumed KV-cache warmup for relatively short sequences. Under the sustained long-sequence traffic pattern from Brightline (video transcript requests), an edge-case in the fallback caused an internal exception which triggered aggressive resource reclamation on a narrow set of Dedicated nodes. That reclamation caused some in-flight requests to fail with 5xx.

Updated action (new):
- Robustness guard: we added an explicit check in the runtime that prevents enter/exit of the experimental kernel for any node running an active long-sequence workload until a full warmup probe passes (Jonas / merged 2026-06-30 22:45Z). This reduces the risk of re-entry.
- Post-deploy canary: added a canary rule that runs long-sequence probes at >5% traffic for 24 hours when we change kernel-selection heuristics (Jonas / in progress, ETA 2026-07-04).

Logs / evidence: we retained the full per-request traces for the incident window and have shared relevant snippets in the Drive folder. If Brightline needs additional request payloads for triage, we can arrange a secure transfer under your consent.

If you want, we can walk these details during the scheduled deep-dive.

Jonas
VP, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
